performance.note: one machine, one bounded observation; not a soak or cross-machine claim

mainFindings: The download contract (`UsageObservationDownloadSchema`) verifies text/bytes/fileName/rows but never recomputes `sha256` from `text`: a producer could advertise a wrong digest and the contract would still accept it. G's tests assert the advertised digest is correct; the contract itself does not.

An envelope whose own fields contradict each other is refused by the schema before the route's scope check runs, so that case returns 400 rather than 503. Both refuse, but the status differs and a client should not rely on 503 alone.

The served DTO still uses the literal `product` in its metric id for a layer-less row (G maps it explicitly) and its header `coverageState` still folds any partial row into `partial`. G did not change main.
notReached: R2 installed package and E verdict for these bytes: no tar carries main 303b2c6a yet; installedAdmission false
R1 download: genuinely absent in 829RC — the package has no route, no method and no library export for it
operator long-term history, model cost baseline and value/benefit: NOT_TESTED; no comparison or benefit figure is produced
actual_native execution: NOT_TESTED — the controlled fixture driver ran; no vendor model or native turn was performed
browser rendering of the download control: main/F own it; G verified the transport contract and the file, not the UI
limitations: A display document has no numeric values by construction; the support summary carries metadata only.
The numeric export still needs an authorization-scoped analysis summary; it is not derived from the served strings.
Snapshot identity is the analysis summary id: two readers of the same window produce different ids and are compared row-wise, not claimed identical.
Agreement in a cross-check is bounded by the coordinator's one-decimal rounding; a larger difference is a disagreement.
review.activeMs stays a partial UI-visibility proxy; unknown usage/cost stay unknown.
